actionItems: Speaker 3 to present next slide with specific, actionable feature list and remote design concepts by end of week
User Interface team to evaluate button mapping, tactile feedback, and mode switching usability by next meeting
Team to assess production cost of modular casing and color packs for subgroup adaptations by next meeting
keyPoints: Remote limited to single device control; no multi-device or whole-house functionality due to budget and time constraints
Core features: power on/off, volume, channel, timer, child lock, and clock display; all within existing circuit
Design emphasizes simplicity, visibility, and impulse appeal with fluorescent buttons, light emission, and beep on multi-press
Modular casing with interchangeable cosmetic covers (colors, shapes) enables cost-effective customization for elderly, children, and adults
Final price point set at €25 to drive impulse purchase; marketing slogan proposed as 'Fashion in electronics'
No teletext or complex systems included; higher management directives exclude outdated or high-risk features
summary.summary: The team finalizes a single, simple remote control for Christmas 2024 launch at €25, focusing on impulse purchase appeal. It includes core features like TV control, volume, channel, timer, child lock, and a clock display, with no multi-device or whole-house support. Design prioritizes simplicity, visibility, and usability, featuring fluorescent buttons, light emission, and a beep on multi-button press. A modular casing allows cosmetic and functional variations for different user groups—children, elderly, and adults—without changing core electronics, keeping costs under budget.
summary.title: Remote Control Design Decisions
